- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) and news volume is high, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 30d horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior 7d high), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (Δsentiment < -1.0) within 5 days, model overcorrects; reduce forecast by 1–4% to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is neutral or bearish (≤0.0) and news volume is low, model underestimates; add 0.5–2% to forecast to avoid underreaction.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 30% of 30d moving average, model is biased low; adjust upward by 1–3%.
- If sentiment change is negative and news volume is rising, model tends to lag; add 0.5–2% to forecast to catch momentum.
- When sentiment is volatile (Δsentiment > 1.0 or < -1.0) over 3–5 days, model overfits; smooth forecast by 1–3% to reduce noise.
